alignments.note: Interrogative particle takes the fronted auxiliary, which is also the clause's question word (rules 17, 20).

Compound preposition rendered by the fixed English phrase *as ... wilt*, discontinuous around the suffix's own pronoun (rule 25). No English word here realizes מִן or עִם's own lexeme, so rule 24's fixed-phrase sentence governs the target head: dropping *wilt* leaves *as thou* saying nothing while *as* is the connective English spends on the relation, exactly as `מִן` → *of one piece with* heads on *piece*. The competing reading heads on *as* as the word carrying the relation. The source head is the governing first morpheme (rule 23).
Suffix as pronoun; rule 30 keeps a suffix outside the fusion of a preposition with its host (rule 18).
The finite verb is recast as an English noun with the clause's copula; head on the word carrying the lexeme.

The object suffix is realized by the object pronoun the ASV writes in the recast subordinate clause (rules 18, 25). The competing reading leaves the suffix unrepresented under rule 22 and marks *it* an added object under rule 44.
Explicit subject pronoun takes only its own English (rule 20).
Verb with its modal; head on the lexical verb (rule 24).
Waw rendered by the connective *Therefore* (rule 14's open list).
No suffix or other possessive morpheme licenses the supplied *his*; the only suffix in the clause is the 3fs object נָּה, realized by *it* (rule 18's closing sentence).

review_notes: Corrected: only the target head of the מֵעִמְּךָ unit moves, from the connective *as* to the content word *wilt*, under rule 24's sentence on a fixed English phrase in which no word realizes the morpheme's own lexeme. Edges, statuses and source heads are unchanged.

*it* was read as the object suffix of יְשַׁלְמֶנָּה realized in the recast subordinate clause; the competing reading leaves the suffix unrepresented and the pronoun added, and is named in that unit's note.
